# 7-Day Family Meal Plan for Mexico City

A simple, budget-conscious plan for 4 people in Mexico City using common supermarket ingredients. It keeps meals flexible so the vegetarian child and lactose-intolerant adult can eat the same base dishes with small swaps.

## Week Menu and Cost Fit

| Day | Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner | Est. Day Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | Oatmeal with banana, cinnamon, peanuts | Chicken tinga tacos with beans and salsa | Veggie quesadillas, salad, avocado | MXN 380 |
| 2 | Eggs with tortillas and fruit | Rice bowls: chicken, beans, corn, pico de gallo | Lentil soup with toast and cucumber | MXN 360 |
| 3 | Chilaquiles with egg or beans | Tuna tostadas for adults, bean tostadas for child | Fajita-style peppers with rice and black beans | MXN 390 |
| 4 | Peanut butter banana sandwiches | Turkey or chicken sandwiches, carrots, fruit | Pasta with tomato sauce and sautéed vegetables | MXN 370 |
| 5 | Oatmeal with apple and raisins | Chicken quesadillas, beans, lettuce | Potato and carrot stew with tortillas | MXN 360 |
| 6 | Huevos a la mexicana with tortillas | Rice and bean burrito bowls | Fish tacos for adults, mushroom tacos for child | MXN 410 |
| 7 | Fruit, toast, and eggs | Leftover chicken/bean soup with tortillas | Simple pozole-style chicken soup, cabbage, radish | MXN 470 |

## Daily Meal Plan

### Day 1
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Breakfast: Oatmeal cooked with water, topped with banana, cinnamon, and peanuts.
- Lunch: Chicken tinga tacos for the adults; use beans and avocado for the vegetarian child.
- Dinner: Cheese-free veggie quesadillas with mushrooms, zucchini, and corn tortillas; serve with salad and avocado.
- Budget tip: Make the tinga sauce once and use it again later in the week.

### Day 2
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/egg-fried.svg
- Breakfast: Scrambled eggs with tortillas and sliced fruit.
- Lunch: Rice bowls with shredded chicken, beans, corn, and pico de gallo.
- Dinner: Lentil soup with carrots, onion, garlic, and toast.
- Budget tip: Cook extra rice and lentils for later meals.

### Day 3
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Breakfast: Chilaquiles with salsa; add egg for the adults, beans for the child.
- Lunch: Tuna tostadas for the adults; bean tostadas for the child and lactose-intolerant adult.
- Dinner: Bell pepper and onion fajitas with rice and black beans.
- Budget tip: Use canned tuna only once to keep costs down.

### Day 4
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/basket.svg
- Breakfast: Peanut butter and banana sandwiches, plus coffee or tea.
- Lunch: Chicken or turkey sandwiches with lettuce, tomato, and carrots.
- Dinner: Pasta in tomato sauce with sautéed zucchini and onion.
- Budget tip: Choose plain pasta and stretch the sauce with vegetables.

### Day 5
- Breakfast: Oatmeal with diced apple, raisins, and cinnamon.
- Lunch: Chicken quesadillas for the adults; bean quesadillas for the child.
- Dinner: Potato and carrot stew with tortillas and salsa.
- Budget tip: Keep cheese optional and separate for the lactose-intolerant adult.

### Day 6
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/fire.svg
- Breakfast: Huevos a la mexicana with tomatoes, onion, and chile, served with tortillas.
- Lunch: Rice and bean burrito bowls with lettuce, salsa, and avocado.
- Dinner: Fish tacos for the adults; mushroom tacos for the child.
- Budget tip: Use frozen fish fillets if they are cheaper than fresh.

### Day 7
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock-history.svg
- Breakfast: Toast, fruit, and eggs.
- Lunch: Leftover chicken and bean soup with tortillas.
- Dinner: Simple pozole-style chicken soup with cabbage, radish, onion, and oregano.
- Budget tip: Use leftovers here to avoid waste and stay within budget.

## Consolidated Shopping List

### Proteins
- Eggs: 24–30
- Chicken thighs or leg quarters: 2.5–3 kg
- Ground or shredded chicken for tinga: included in chicken total
- Canned tuna: 2 cans
- Frozen fish fillets: 700 g to 1 kg
- Dry lentils: 1 kg
- Dry black or pinto beans: 1.5 kg
- Peanut butter: 1 jar

### Grains and Staples
- Corn tortillas: 5–6 kg total or equivalent packs
- White rice: 2 kg
- Oats: 1.5 kg
- Pasta: 1 kg
- Bread: 2 loaves
- Tostadas: 1–2 packs

### Vegetables
- Tomatoes: 2.5–3 kg
- Onions: 1.5 kg
- Garlic: 2 heads
- Carrots: 1.5 kg
- Potatoes: 2 kg
- Zucchini: 1.5 kg
- Bell peppers: 6–8
- Lettuce or cabbage: 2 heads
- Cucumber: 2
- Radishes: 2 bunches
- Mushrooms: 500–700 g
- Corn: 4–6 ears or 2 cans
- Avocados: 6–8
- Limes: 12–16
- Cilantro: 3 bunches

### Fruit
- Bananas: 14–18
- Apples: 6–8
- Oranges or seasonal fruit: 8–10

### Dairy and Lactose-Free Swaps
- Cheese: 400–500 g for those who eat it
- Lactose-free milk or plant milk: 2–3 liters
- Yogurt: optional, only if budget allows and lactose-free version is preferred

### Pantry and Flavor
- Cooking oil
- Salt
- Black pepper
- Cinnamon
- Dried oregano
- Ground cumin
- Chile powder or salsa
- Tomato sauce or passata: 2–3 cartons/cans
- Vinegar

## Budget Estimate

| Category | Estimated Cost |
|---|---:|
| Proteins | MXN 1,050 |
| Grains and staples | MXN 650 |
| Vegetables | MXN 650 |
| Fruit | MXN 250 |
| Dairy and swaps | MXN 150 |
| Pantry and seasonings | MXN 50 |
| **Total** | **MXN 2,800** |

## Practical Notes

- Keep the same base meal for everyone, then split toppings: cheese on the side, beans for the vegetarian child, and meat for the two meat-eaters.
- Use tortillas, rice, beans, and oats as the main budget anchors.
- Buy seasonal produce at local supermarkets or neighborhood markets for lower prices.
- If prices run high, reduce fish to one meal and replace it with eggs or beans.
